subject: FinApp procurement: uptime floor & monthly credit buckets
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finapp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
Cc: procurement@finapp.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood SLA: baseline uptimes and credit caps (initial redlines)

Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — FinApp is excited about Redwood's latency profile for our conversational agents. Our procurement/legal team took a pass at the standard SLA and pushed back on two items we want to surface:

1) Uptime baseline: we prefer a 99.95% monthly uptime commitment for hosted workloads.
2) Monthly credit cap: we typically need higher out-of-the-box credit relief if the floor is above 99.9% — our procurement team is uncomfortable with a very low cap for enterprise incidents.

Attached is our initial redline (FinApp_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf) which proposes: 99.95% uptime; credit buckets that scale with spend (up to 50% of monthly invoice in severe months). We understand this is above Redwood's public template, so please let me know if you have counterproposals or constraints around credit caps.

Additionally, we care about a 95th percentile latency SLO for inference calls (tail latency guarantees for sync endpoints). If you can point me to how Redwood measures and enforces this, that would help move procurement.

Timeline: procurement is hoping to get to signature by next Friday (2027-05-21) if we can agree the core economics.

Best,
Alex
Alex Torres
Head of Procurement, FinApp

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA: baseline uptimes and credit caps (initial redlines)

Alex — thanks for the clear redlines and the timeline. We value FinApp as a strategic customer and want to land something that balances your reliability needs with our ability to operate predictable capacity.

Quick take:
- Uptime: our standard hosted SLA for PLG/Enterprise is 99.9% monthly. We can consider 99.95% for an enterprise contract if we agree to a scaled credit schedule and a higher committed spend / dedicated capacity clause.
- Credits: we typically cap monthly credits at a percentage of monthly fees to avoid open-ended exposure. That said, we can propose tiered buckets that increase with spend tiers (e.g., higher caps for higher commitments).
- Latency: our measurement is server-side, 95th percentile over a 30-day window per endpoint variant; we can provide a statement of measurement methodology and sample dashboards. Tail latency commitments for synchronous endpoints are possible but require alignment on payload sizes, model variant, and batching expectations.

I attached a proposed credit schedule that could be a middle ground: higher caps for customers committing to a dedicated capacity or a 12-month reserved plan. See attachment: RWI_proposed_credit_schedule_20270514.pdf.

Next steps: 1) Karthik, can you take point on commercial handshake (spend/commitment)? 2) Marissa, can you coordinate an engineering note that explains our latency measurement and the carveouts for queued/batched traffic? 3) Ben, can you confirm finance comfort with the proposed buckets?

I'll wait for a short counter from your side and can set a 30-min alignment call today or tomorrow.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Principal Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redwood SLA: baseline uptimes and credit caps (initial redlines)

KF team — quick internal thread before we reply to FinApp.

Kimberly, thanks for the draft. My read: FinApp wants both a higher uptime and a meaningful monthly credit cap. We should aim for a pragmatic compromise that:
- preserves our economic exposure (cap scaled to committed ARR or dedicated pool),
- gives FinApp confidence (higher floor + explicit latency measurement), and
- avoids operational risk from overly broad carveouts.

Proposed internal counter (short):
- Offer: 99.95% uptime only if FinApp signs a 12-month reserved commitment for a dedicated pool OR agrees to a spend threshold (e.g., >= $50k/mo).
- Credits: tiered cap: up to 25% of monthly invoice for < $50k spend; up to 40% for $50k-150k; up to 60% only if dedicated capacity and a 12-month commitment.
- Latency: provide a measurement statement and commit to 95th percentile SLO for a bounded request size (<=2k tokens) on hosted endpoints; exclude periods where customer enables non-production load testing or has misconfigured batching.

Marissa — if engineering can confirm the 95th percentile measurement approach and exception language by EOD, I'll push this as our counter to Alex and propose a short ’commercial quid-pro-quo’ in exchange for the higher cap (e.g., faster support SLA response times).

Ben — flag any finance concerns on the caps; we should avoid uncapped exposure.

— Karthik

Subject: Re: Redwood SLA: baseline uptimes and credit caps (initial redlines)

Kimberly — appreciate the thoughtful counter and the credit schedule. Procurement discussed the proposed trade (99.95% tied to committed spend / dedicated pool) and we're willing to accept that structure on the following points:

1) Scheduled maintenance carveout: FinApp needs an explicit maximum monthly maintenance window (we propose <= 4 hours/month) and advance notice (>= 72 hours) for non-emergency maintenance. Credits should not apply to emergency maintenance with documented outage causes, but planned maintenance should be distinct and limited.
2) Measurement transparency: provide a read-only dashboard link or weekly CSV export with uptime/latency measurements so our platform ops can validate metrics during the procurement review.
3) Execution: we will route the final redline to our legal e-sign flow once we get the updated redline reflecting the carveout language.

I've attached an updated redline (FinApp_SLA_Redlines_v2.pdf) that inserts the scheduled maintenance window and requests a DocuSign. If you can send the updated version with the proposed tiered caps (your RWI_proposed_credit_schedule) and the measurement statement, procurement will run for signature next week.

Thanks — can we get the updated package by Monday EOD?

Alex
Head of Procurement, FinApp
